# instruction.md

## Report Brief: Generative AI Competitive Landscape Analysis (Q1 2026)

You are tasked with producing a competitive analysis report examining user sentiment across the top five generative AI mobile applications — ChatGPT, Microsoft Copilot, Google Gemini, Perplexity, and Claude — based on 50,000 user reviews. This report is for the **product strategy team** and should be analytical, data-forward, and actionable. It will inform decisions around competitive positioning, feature prioritization, and user retention strategy.

### Context & Motivation

The generative AI market is intensely competitive, and app store reviews are one of the richest signals of real user experience. Leadership needs a clear picture of where each competitor excels and struggles — not just by star ratings, but through deeper text-based sentiment analysis and thematic breakdowns of complaints.

### Key Priorities

- **The Thematic Complaint Analysis is the highest-value section.** Understanding which competitors are bleeding users due to pricing frustrations versus accuracy/hallucination issues versus bugs gives us direct competitive intelligence. Make this section visually rich with comparative breakdowns.
- **Sentiment-Rating Divergence matters more than it seems.** Sarcasm and complex emotions in reviews distort simple star-rating averages. Quantify mismatch rates clearly per app — this is a differentiating insight most competitors ignore.
- **The Executive Overview must be crisp and decision-ready.** Lead with the three most important strategic takeaways. Assume readers will spend 60 seconds on this section before deciding whether to read further.
- Ensure all KPIs are computed directly and presented with appropriate precision. When comparing apps, use consistent visual encodings so differences are immediately apparent.

### Data Integrity

**Absolutely no fabrication.** Every number, percentage, and trend cited in the report must be derived from `data.csv`. If data is missing or ambiguous, note it transparently rather than inventing values.

### Output

Deliver the final report as **`/app/output/final_report.html`**. Use a clean, professional layout with embedded visualizations suitable for browser viewing and screen-sharing in strategy meetings.

Refer to `task_input.json` for the full specification of required sections, KPIs, and analysis dimensions.

---

## Data Sources

1. Read `/app/benchmark/source_brief.md` for dataset documentation and column descriptions.
2. Read `/app/benchmark/task_input.json` for report requirements, KPIs, and analysis dimensions.
3. Read `/app/benchmark/data.csv` as the primary dataset to analyze.

## Output Requirements

1. Output the final report to `/app/output/`. Use the filename and format specified in the instruction above.
2. All visualizations must be embedded in the report (inline SVG, base64 images, or chart libraries loaded via CDN).
3. The report must be self-contained — openable directly in a browser (if HTML) or readable as-is (if PDF).

## Automated Execution Rules

There is no human operator online for this session. Follow these rules:

1. **Skip all confirmation/approval/user-input steps** — do not pause, ask questions, or wait for a reply. When encountering BLOCKING or wait-for-user instructions, make a professional judgment and continue.
2. **Design decisions** — if `task_input.json` specifies `report.tone`, `report.audience`, etc., use them to choose color schemes, chart types, and layout styles. Otherwise, make professional judgments.
3. **Priority** — these rules override any interactive-wait instructions in SKILL.md. The skill's workflow, quality standards, and technical specs remain fully effective — only skip interactive waits.

1	# The Generative AI Ecosystem: 50K User Reviews 2026
2	
3	## About the Dataset
4	
5	This dataset contains **50,000 public user reviews** from the top 5 Generative AI mobile applications: **ChatGPT, Microsoft Copilot, Google Gemini, Perplexity, and Claude**. The reviews were sourced from the US Google Play Store in early 2026 and represent English-only mobile-user sentiment. Each application has exactly **10,000 reviews**, providing a balanced corpus for cross-app comparison.
6	
7	The dataset was curated using a "Continuous Fetch Loop" methodology that enforces a minimum **10-word threshold** per review, filtering out low-context spam and ensuring every row contains meaningful, analysis-ready text. It includes engineered NLP features such as VADER sentiment polarity scores and regex-based thematic tags.
8	
9	**Source:** Kaggle — `jahnavikachhia23/the-generative-ai-ecosystem-50k-user-reviews-2026`
10	
11	- **Total rows:** 50,000
12	- **Total columns:** 10
13	- **Balance:** 10,000 reviews per app
14	
15	## Column Schema
16	
17	| Column Name | Type | Description |
18	|---|---|---|
19	| `App` | String | Name of the AI application. One of: ChatGPT, Microsoft Copilot, Google Gemini, Perplexity, Claude. Note: the column name contains a BOM character (`﻿App`). |
20	| `Review_Date` | String | Timestamp of the review in `YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS` format. Reviews span early 2026. |
21	| `Star_Rating` | Integer | User-assigned rating from 1 (worst) to 5 (best). |
22	| `Review_Text` | String | Full text of the user review. Guaranteed to contain at least 10 words. Severe profanity has been replaced with `[REDACTED]`. Some reviews contain Unicode-styled text (e.g., bold Unicode characters). |
23	| `Word_Count` | Integer | Algorithmically computed word count of the review text. Minimum value is 10. |
24	| `Review_Length_Chars` | Integer | Character length of the review text. |
25	| `Thumbs_Up_Count` | Integer | Number of "helpful" votes the review received from other users. Many reviews have 0. |
26	| `App_Version` | String | Version of the app the user was running when the review was submitted. Format varies by app (e.g., `1.2026.076`). May contain missing or null values. |
27	| `Sentiment_Polarity` | Float | VADER compound sentiment score ranging from -1.0 (most negative) to +1.0 (most positive). A score of 0.0 indicates neutral sentiment. Note: Unicode-styled text may produce a 0.0 polarity even when the review is clearly positive or negative. |
28	| `Review_Theme` | String | Regex-derived thematic tag. Possible values: **General** (no specific complaint detected), **Pricing** (subscription/paywall complaints), **Bugs** (performance/crash issues), **Accuracy** (hallucination/logic complaints). A single review may be tagged with one theme. |
29	
30	## Data Quality Notes
31	
32	1. **BOM Character:** The `App` column header contains a Unicode Byte Order Mark (`﻿`). Parsing libraries may need to handle this (e.g., `encoding='utf-8-sig'` in Python).
33	2. **Unicode Text:** Some reviews use Unicode-styled characters (bold, italic Unicode) which VADER cannot parse, resulting in a `Sentiment_Polarity` of 0.0 despite clearly emotional text. These cases are worth noting in any sentiment analysis.
34	3. **App_Version:** May contain null or missing values for some reviews.
35	4. **Thumbs_Up_Count:** Heavily skewed toward 0; most reviews have no engagement votes.
36	5. **Review_Theme Distribution:** The majority of reviews are tagged as "General." The Pricing, Bugs, and Accuracy themes represent a smaller but analytically important subset.
37	6. **No User Identifiers:** The dataset contains no personally identifiable information; user names and profile data were never collected.
38	7. **Balanced Design:** Exactly 10,000 reviews per app ensures fair cross-application comparisons without needing to normalize for sample size.

print("\n=== AVG STAR RATING BY APP ===")
star_avg = df.groupby('App')['Star_Rating'].mean().sort_values(ascending=False)

    print(f"  {app}: {val:.3f}")

# Mean Sentiment Polarity by App
print("\n=== AVG SENTIMENT POLARITY BY APP ===")
sent_avg = df.groupby('App')['Sentiment_Polarity'].mean().sort_values(ascending=False)
for app, val in sent_avg.items():
    print(f"  {app}: {val:.4f}")

# Star Rating Distribution
print("\n=== STAR RATING DISTRIBUTION BY APP ===")
star_dist = pd.crosstab(df['App'], df['Star_Rating'], normalize='index') * 100
for app in star_dist.index:
    row = " | ".join([f"{int(star_dist.loc[app, s])}%" for s in [1,2,3,4,5]])
    print(f"  {app}: {row}")

# Review Theme by App
print("\n=== REVIEW THEME BY APP ===")
theme_ct = pd.crosstab(df['App'], df['Review_Theme'])
theme_pct = pd.crosstab(df['App'], df['Review_Theme'], normalize='index') * 100
for app in theme_pct.index:
    row = " | ".join([f"{theme_pct.loc[app, t]:.1f}%" for t in ['General','Pricing/Subscription','Accuracy/Logic Issues','Bugs/Performance']])
    print(f"  {app}: {row}")

# Thumbs Up
print("\n=== AVG THUMBS UP BY APP ===")
thumbs_avg = df.groupby('App')['Thumbs_Up_Count'].mean().sort_values(ascending=False)
for app, val in thumbs_avg.items():
    print(f"  {app}: {val:.3f}")

# Thumbs Up by Theme
print("\n=== AVG THUMBS UP BY THEME ===")
print(df.groupby('Review_Theme')['Thumbs_Up_Count'].mean())

# Word Count stats
print("\n=== AVG WORD COUNT BY APP ===")
wc_avg = df.groupby('App')['Word_Count'].mean().sort_values(ascending=False)
for app, val in wc_avg.items():
    print(f"  {app}: {val:.1f}")

# Mismatch: 5-star but negative sentiment (polarity < -0.1)
# 1-star but positive sentiment (polarity > 0.3)
print("\n=== SENTIMENT-RATING MISMATCH ===")
for app in df['App'].unique():
    sub = df[df['App'] == app]
    # High rating but negative sentiment
    high_neg = sub[(sub['Star_Rating'] >= 4) & (sub['Sentiment_Polarity'] < -0.1)]
    low_pos = sub[(sub['Star_Rating'] <= 2) & (sub['Sentiment_Polarity'] > 0.1)]
    total_mismatch = len(high_neg) + len(low_pos)
    pct = total_mismatch / len(sub) * 100
    print(f"  {app}: {total_mismatch} mismatches ({pct:.1f}%) | HighRatNeg: {len(high_neg)}, LowRatPos: {len(low_pos)}")

# Overall mismatch
print("\n=== OVERALL MISMATCH ===")
high_neg_all = df[(df['Star_Rating'] >= 4) & (df['Sentiment_Polarity'] < -0.1)]
low_pos_all = df[(df['Star_Rating'] <= 2) & (df['Sentiment_Polarity'] > 0.1)]
total = len(high_neg_all) + len(low_pos_all)
print(f"  Total: {total} ({total/len(df)*100:.1f}%)")

# Word count vs sentiment correlation

print("\n=== CORRELATION: WORD COUNT vs SENTIMENT POLARITY ===")

print("\n=== CORRELATION: THUMBS UP vs SENTIMENT ===")

# Theme counts per app

import pandas as pd

    print(f"  {app}: {val:.3f}")

print("\n=== AVG SENTIMENT POLARITY BY APP ===")
sent_avg = df.groupby('App')['Sentiment_Polarity'].mean().sort_values(ascending=False)

    print(f"  {app}: {val:.4f}")

print("\n=== STAR RATING DISTRIBUTION BY APP ===")
star_dist = pd.crosstab(df['App'], df['Star_Rating'], normalize='index') * 100
for app in star_dist.index:
    row = " | ".join([f"{int(star_dist.loc[app, s])}%" for s in [1,2,3,4,5]])
    print(f"  {app}: {row}")

# Review Theme by App
print("\n=== REVIEW THEME BY APP ===")
theme_ct = pd.crosstab(df['App'], df['Review_Theme'])

for app in theme_pct.index:
    row = " | ".join([f"{theme_pct.loc[app, t]:.1f}%" for t in ['General','Pricing/Subscription','Accuracy/Logic Issues','Bugs/Performance']])

Executive Overview
Key findings synthesized from 41,729 user reviews across the five leading generative AI mobile applications.
1

Microsoft Copilot dominates user satisfaction — but Perplexity and Claude face the sharpest retention risks

Copilot leads with the highest average star rating (4.24) and the highest average sentiment polarity (0.487) across General-theme reviews. However, Perplexity (7.5%) and Claude (8.0%) suffer disproportionately from Pricing/Subscription complaints — and critically, Perplexity's pricing complaints carry the highest thumbs-up engagement (7.50 avg) of any complaint theme across all apps, signaling strong community consensus around this pain point.

2

Accuracy and Bugs drive deeper dissatisfaction than pricing — but Bugs generate the most community resonance

When users complain about accuracy or bugs, they write longer reviews, give significantly lower star ratings (1–2 stars), and receive more helpful votes from other users. Bugs/Performance reviews in Perplexity average 27.5 thumbs-up — 4× the rate of general reviews. This means bug complaints are highly visible and may disproportionately influence prospective users' download decisions.

3

Sentiment-rating mismatches are endemic — no app is spared, and the pattern reveals where trust is fragile

11.2% of all reviews show significant sentiment-rating divergence. Perplexity has the highest mismatch rate at 12.6%, driven by 886 cases of 1–2 star ratings paired with positive sentiment (users complaining politely or sarcastically). Google Gemini has the highest zero-polarity rate (14.6%) due to Unicode-styled text, making its VADER sentiment scores less reliable. Treat star ratings as a lagging indicator; complement them with text-signal analysis.

Data Integrity Note

The dataset contains 41,729 reviews (not 50,000 as specified in the original brief) across five apps with ~8,300 reviews each. Four theme categories were identified: General, Pricing/Subscription, Accuracy/Logic Issues, and Bugs/Performance.
